discovery: Cavity optomechanics: quantum control of macroscopic mechanical motion by radiation pressure

nominees.name: Markus Aspelmeyer
nominees.affiliation: University of Vienna and IQOQI Vienna, Austrian Academy of Sciences, Austria

nominees.name: Tobias J. Kippenberg
nominees.affiliation: École Polytechnique Fédérale de Lausanne (EPFL), Switzerland

motivation: Radiation pressure, long only a limit on precision measurement, was made into a tool for controlling mechanical motion at the quantum level. Vahala and Kippenberg showed that high-Q optical microresonators have strong optomechanical coupling, with dynamical backaction amplification and cooling. Aspelmeyer's and Kippenberg's groups demonstrated radiation-pressure self-cooling and sideband cooling of micro-mechanical oscillators. These experiments led to the optical ground-state cooling of mechanical modes, strong coupling, optomechanically induced transparency, squeezing and entanglement between light and massive objects. The field they founded gives quantum-limited force and displacement sensing, interfaces between microwave and optical quantum systems, and new tests of quantum mechanics with increasingly massive objects, including proposed probes of gravity's quantum nature. It extends the quantum control of light and atoms to the macroscopic mechanical world, with broad conceptual and technological impact.
